common_name: Monarch Madness Pink Joe Pye Weed

planting.note: Set out container divisions in spring or fall in average to moist soil; this North Creek Nurseries introduction flowers along the entire stem rather than just at the tips, giving a fuller, shrub-like bloom display.

directions: Give this Joe Pye weed selection consistently moist to average soil in a rain garden, pond margin, or large perennial border where its mature size can be accommodated. Deep wine-red spring growth matures to green stems topped from late summer into fall with huge dome-shaped clusters of rosy-pink flowers that cover nearly the whole plant rather than just the crown. Leave the dried flower heads standing through winter for songbirds and cut the clump back in late winter before new growth starts. It is deer-resistant and draws heavy traffic from butterflies and native bees during its long bloom season.

common_name: Monarch Madness White Joe Pye Weed

planting.note: Set out container divisions in spring or fall in average to moist soil; the white-flowered sibling to Monarch Madness Pink, from North Creek Nurseries.

directions: This white sibling to Monarch Madness Pink produces the same enormous, dome-shaped flower clusters but in pure white, held above clean green foliage from late summer through fall. Plant in average to moist soil at a pond edge, rain garden, or mixed border, giving it room to reach full height without staking. Monarchs, swallowtails, and native bees work the flowers heavily right up until frost, and the seed heads then feed songbirds through winter. It is deer-resistant and needs only an annual late-winter cutback to stay tidy.

planting.note: Plant container plugs in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; part of the Free Spirit grasses collection bred by Hortech, Inc. and distributed through Darwin Perennials.

directions: Blue Arrow forms a tight, narrow, upright clump of fine blades holding a crisp, steel-blue color through the growing season, making it a strong vertical accent without the floppiness of older little bluestem selections. Plant in lean, well-drained soil in full sun, where drainage and light together keep the color saturated and the habit from splaying open. It tolerates drought and poor soil once rooted in and needs no fertilizer or staking. Cut the whole clump to the ground in late winter before new blue growth emerges.

planting.note: Plant container plugs in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; a Free Spirit collection little bluestem valued for multi-season color change.

directions: Comet stands out among little bluestem selections for its upright habit and dramatic seasonal color shift, opening sky blue in early summer and moving through ruby red, purple, and green tones as the season progresses. Site it in lean, well-drained soil in full sun so the clump stays upright and the color sequence develops fully. Once established it shrugs off drought and poor soil, asking only for a hard cutback in late winter. Use it as a changing seasonal accent in mixed borders or massed prairie-style plantings.

planting.note: Plant container plugs in spring in lean, well-drained soil in full sun; a vase-shaped Free Spirit collection little bluestem topped with silver plumes in fall.

directions: Mystic Purple holds a distinctive vase-shaped habit, with blades that deepen into purple and red tones over the season and top out in fall with airy silver plumes that catch low light beautifully. Give it lean, well-drained soil and full sun, since rich or wet ground causes the clump to flop and lose its upright vase form. It is drought-tolerant and low-maintenance once established, needing just an annual cutback to the ground in late winter. Works well as a textural specimen or repeated through a native-style border.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring or fall in humus-rich, consistently moist soil; a Proven Winners refinement of the original Invincibelle Wee White with a denser, more floriferous habit and a minimum of six hours of bright sun recommended.

directions: This improved dwarf smooth hydrangea keeps the true small scale of the original Wee White but builds an even denser, more mounded habit covered in white flowers that age to soft green from summer through fall. Plant in humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist, giving at least six hours of bright sun with afternoon shade in hot climates to protect the blooms. Because it flowers on new wood, a hard cutback in late winter sacrifices nothing and keeps the mound tight and floriferous. Its true-dwarf size suits small borders, mass plantings, and large containers where full-size Annabelle types would overwhelm the space.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after frost danger passes into well-drained, fertile soil or containers; a Proven Winners double-flowered Superbells release.

directions: Superbells Double Mardi Gras produces fully doubled, ruffled flowers in lavender-purple splashed with streaks of yellow and white, giving a carnival-like look distinct from single-flowered calibrachoa. Grow it in containers or hanging baskets in part sun to full sun, using a well-drained potting mix and consistent fertilization since the double blooms are heavier feeders than singles. It blooms early in the season and keeps going without deadheading, dropping spent flowers cleanly. Pinch lightly after the first flush to encourage fuller branching and continued bloom through summer.

planting.note: Set out vegetatively propagated starts after frost danger passes into well-drained, fertile soil or containers; a corrected re-release of the original Supertunia Bordeaux bred to resolve foliar distortion and blind-shoot issues seen in the earlier version.

directions: Supertunia Bordeaux II carries slightly lighter lavender flowers with dark veining and an occasional white picotee edge, an updated version bred to grow out cleanly where the original Bordeaux sometimes showed distorted foliage or non-flowering shoots. Plant in part sun to full sun in well-drained, fertile soil or a container mix, and feed regularly to sustain its spreading, mounded habit through the season. It blooms earlier in spring than the original and holds up better to heat and weather swings. Trim back lightly if it becomes leggy in midsummer to refresh flowering through fall.
